verdictLine: NOT CLOSED: R4-1, a regression against 9822af0 that R3-3 introduced (the possessive skip also reaches decideDouble(), so in en-GB single-outer and nl a straight inch mark inside a curly ‘ quotation turns into a closing ’ when a plural possessive follows). A contained fix is shown by a probe. R3-1, R3-2, R3-4, R3-5 and R3-6 are closed; R3-3 is regressed (R4-1). Follow-ups R4-2 to R4-6.

R3-1.evidence:
Every input in gate-q8w3/word.tsv and word2.tsv, and the ‘hood, ‘80s, ‘til and ‘em rows of prose.tsv, gives its 9822af0 output in typed and depth (e.g.

"Back in the ‘90s we had fun," she said. "Yes," he said.

→ “Back in the ‘90s we had fun,” she said. “Yes,” he said.). It also holds through Lite’s |sorts filter in the testbed. My own prose (gate-x5n4/prose-own.tsv: ‘70s, ‘til, ‘em, ‘80s in en-US, en-GB, de ‚80ern, es ‘80, nl double-outer ‘s avonds) gives 9822af0’s output on every wrong-way-apostrophe row. Load-bearing: restoring R2-2’s pop kind alone (t/U-BO) fails 22 cases, the 12 r3-1-* among them. The 12 r2-2-* cases now pin the back-out (the Known-limit glyph), as D843 decided. The fixer’s 50-line dlg.tsv differs from 9822af0 on one row only (fi 15" → 15″, an intended R2-1 change).

R3-2.evidence: sv ”Det kostar 5", sa han. ”Billigt.” → 5”; sv ”Det är rum 101", sa hon, ”eller 102”. → 101”; fi ”Se maksoi 5", hän sanoi. ”Halpa.” → 5”, typed and depth. The R2-1 inch rows stay primes (”Näyttö on 27" leveä”, hän sanoi. ”Liian iso.” → 27″). Undoing R3-2 alone (t/U-R32) fails the 6 r3-2-* cases. Every generated row that R3-2 moves against 03dd4f3 is a closer-at-a-digit row. The parity reads the ”…” pair correctly but cannot see openers of the ’…’ pair (R4-2), and no case pins an odd count above one (R4-3).

R3-3.evidence: The three repro inputs keep ’: ‘The final score was 3' and the players’ bus left early. → 3’; ‘We won 2' – then the fans’ songs began. → 2’; ‘It was room 101' and the guests’ rooms were empty. → 101’. r2-4-foot-inside-curly-single and r2-4-de-foot-inside-curly-nested stay primes. Undoing R3-3 alone (t/U-R33) fails 5 cases; dropping only its multibyte trim (t/U-R33trim) fails r3-3-possessive-look-ahead-ending-inside-a-character. However, the skip sits in closerAhead(), which decideDouble() also calls, so it changes a branch that 9822af0 already had: R4-1. It also does not reach a possessive followed by a tag or an entity, or one inside inline markup (R4-4).

R3-4.evidence: I rebuilt Q2, Q4, Q8 and Q9 against 7823e68 (gate-x5n4/q/; the fixer’s t/Q* trees predate the back-out and its final corpus). Each fails exactly one named case: Q2 r3-4-inch-inside-curly-single-with-no-outer-closer, Q4 r3-4-straight-opened-quotation-is-the-nearest-of-its-kind, Q8 r3-4-de-possessive-look-ahead-cuts-a-4-byte-character, Q9 r3-4-fi-inch-across-a-tag (3855 passed, 1 failed each). gate-kit on the fixer’s r3-mutants.yaml: ok=15, all 13 killed, “ok 123 files + git unchanged  real tree”.

R3-5.evidence: README:330 now says it “can happen in any language” and labels its numbers as one sweep. They reproduce exactly at 7823e68 with recheck-r7v2/idemgen.php seed 7 1500 (gate-x5n4/idem-new-7.txt): apostrophes off 4 (nl) to 15 (en-GB single-outer) per language and mode, fr 38, fr-CH 40 and 43; primes off at most 1; default rules 0.

R3-6.evidence: The README:79 sentence is gone with the back-out, which makes the R3-6 question moot. The new Known limit (README:331) states the mixed-shape case with an example that reproduces: it «Disse “sì" e partì» → «Disse “sì» e partì», typed and depth. SPEC D829 records the back-out under D843. Every other README:79 example still holds (en-GB single-outer ‘She said "no"’ → ‘She said “no”’, de book »›Nein,‹ sagte er«, sv ”Han sa: ’nej.’”, the es guillemets-outer order by the mark typed).

findings.summary:
A regression from R3-3, against both 9822af0 and 03dd4f3. The plural-possessive skip was added inside closerAhead(), which decideDouble() calls as well as decideSingle(). In a locale whose primary pair is ‘…’ (en-GB single-outer and nl), a straight " after a digit inside a curly ‘ quotation that has no closer still to come therefore closes the quotation as ’ whenever a plural possessive follows in the paragraph. The ‘ can be a wrong-way apostrophe (‘s avonds, ‘90s) or a quotation that runs on into the next paragraph. Three examples, typed and depth: nl

‘s Avonds keken we naar een 27" tv in Klaas’ kamer.

→ 27’; en-GB single-outer

‘The new set has a 27" screen, and the players’ lounge has two.

→ 27’; en-GB single-outer

In the ‘90s a 27" telly was bigger than the players’ wages.

→ 27’. 9822af0 and 03dd4f3 give 27″ on all three. In this branch the skip can only do harm: a straight " that really closes a curly ‘ is the mixed-shape case the README now lists as a Known limit. It reproduces through Craft (the testbed’s mounted plugin).

R3-2’s parity cannot see the openers of fi and sv’s ’…’ pair. That pair’s closer is also the apostrophe, so the suffix loop skips a ’ that a letter follows, which is every opener. The count ahead is therefore the number of closers alone, and a foot mark inside ’…’ followed by another ’…’ quotation in the paragraph closes it. sv

’Han är 6' lång’, sa hon. ’Ja.’

→ 6’; sv

”Hon sa ’han är 6' lång’ och ’mycket snäll’”, berättade han.

→ 6’; fi

’Hän on 6' pitkä’, sanoi hän. ’Niin.’

→ 6’; fi ”Hän sanoi ’olen 6' pitkä’ ja ’vahva’” → 6’. 03dd4f3 (R2-1) gave 6′ on all four; 9822af0 gives 6’, so this is no worse than the fallback. It is R2-1 partly undone for the ’ pair, and the ”…” pair is unaffected.

R3-3 does not reach a plural possessive that is followed by a tag or an entity, or that sits inside inline markup. In those cases a straight ' after a digit that really ends a curly ‘…’ is still a foot mark, the R2-4 regression against 9822af0. en-US, typed and depth:

‘The final score was 3' and the players’ bus left early.

→ 3′. 9822af0 gives 3’ on all three; 03dd4f3 gives 3′. Two causes. The 8-byte look-ahead reads raw HTML (a space then < or &). A ’ in a later text node of the flow is counted by countAfter($closePattern), which has no possessive skip. A capitalised word after the possessive (players’ Bus Company) also counts, as decideSingle()’s own possessive test reads it; that is consistent, and fine as a limit. This is not new to round 3 (03dd4f3 is the same) but is left open by it. By the brief’s scope rule it is a follow-up; graded as recheck-2 graded R3-3, it would block.
